results.sentence: Draft internet standard from Anthropic's Kevin Kelley, dated Oct 30, ... __usage_ai-training, Microsoft will honor from Feb 1, 2027, Google aims 2027
results.evidence: Draft: K. Kelley, Anthropic, 30 Oct 2026, token __usage_ai-training. Bing: 'Starting February 1, 2027, Microsoft will honor the new preferences as it crawls'. Google: 'We aim to support this new control ... in 2027'.

results.sentence: UIUC-led preprint: 90 of 99 results from 11 memory systems scored below naive RAG
results.evidence: Project page: '11 evaluated representative memory systems', '90 / 99 memory results below Naive RAG'; first author and senior authors (Han, Zhai) at UIUC. I also counted 90 negative deltas in arXiv Table 1. Note the reference is the stronger 2-round RAG variant (RAG (2rd)).

results.sentence: Qwenputer: 32-bit RISC-V in Qwen 3.5 4B, 97.5% on 40-problem multiplication set vs 55% stock
results.evidence: Blog: mul_big Qwenputer 97.5%, base Qwen 55%; README: 'Greedy decoding, 40 problems per set'.

results.sentence: A draft standard dated Oct 30 defines one shared token: __usage_ai-training
results.evidence: Abstract/Sec 4.1 define the token; dated 30 October 2026.

results.sentence: Draft comes from Kevin Kelley of Anthropic; individual proposal filed with IETF; tracker says 'not endorsed by the IETF'
results.evidence: Datatracker: 'This I-D is not endorsed by the IETF and has no formal standing'; group shown as '(individual)'.

results.sentence: Anthropic, Google and Microsoft have each said they will honor it
results.evidence: Anthropic: 'has already started implementing support' (Kelley's list message). Google: 'announcing our plans to support', 'aim to support ... in 2027'. Microsoft: 'will honor' from Feb 1, 2027. 'Will honor' overstates Anthropic's and Google's wording.
results.fix: Anthropic says it has started implementing support, Google says it plans to support it, and Microsoft says it will honor it from Feb 1, 2027.

results.sentence: Token goes in a robots.txt User-Agent line; 'no new directive names and no new grammar'; older readers skip it
results.evidence: Abstract quote exact; Sec 1: existing parsers 'will ignore policy-token groups as they would any group for a user agent they do not recognize'.

results.sentence: In the draft's example, Disallow: / with Allow: /press-kit/ means no training on the site except its press kit
results.evidence: Draft Fig 1 and text: it 'expresses a preference against AI training for all paths except those under /press-kit/, for which it expresses a preference in favor'. It is a preference, not a rule; elsewhere the draft says it is not a crawl directive.
results.fix: In the draft's example, Disallow: / paired with Allow: /press-kit/ expresses a preference against training everywhere except the press kit, where it expresses a preference in favor.

results.sentence: 'AI training' means 'using an asset to modify the learned parameters of a generative AI model'
results.evidence: Sec 3 quotes the aipref vocab definition verbatim.

results.sentence: Catch-all User-Agent: * group does not apply; a site without the token has expressed no preference
results.evidence: Sec 4.2: wildcard groups MUST NOT match the token; no token group means no preference.

results.sentence: Anthropic 'has already started implementing support for this draft,' per IETF list message
results.evidence: Message from Kelley, 30 Oct 2026: 'Anthropic has already started implementing support for this draft'.

results.sentence: Google: lets owners 'express their AI training preferences across multiple AI providers in a single step'; aims to support 'in 2027'
results.evidence: Both quotes exact in Google's post (posted by John Mueller, Oct 30, 2026).

results.sentence: 'Starting February 1, 2027, Microsoft will honor the new preferences as it crawls'
results.evidence: Exact quote on the Bing blog page.

results.sentence: OpenAI will roll out support 'in the coming months,' per a daily.dev summary of OpenAI's announcement
results.evidence: daily.dev (From openai.com): 'will roll out in the coming months'. Attributed to the secondary source, which is correct. AI Weekly and Vanessa Fox also say OpenAI announced support. I did not open openai.com.

results.sentence: 'We could not read OpenAI's own post.'
results.evidence: This is a process note, not a reader-facing statement. The attribution to daily.dev already carries the caveat.
results.fix: Cut the sentence, or reword as 'OpenAI's own post was not available to us at publication' if the editor wants disclosure.

results.sentence: 'Training and grounding are independent preferences,' Microsoft says
results.evidence: Exact quote in the guide section of the Bing post.

results.sentence: Grounding is when an AI assistant pulls in web pages to answer a question
results.evidence: Bing: grounding 'connects generated responses to web content when an answer is created'. Plain-language gloss is fair.

results.sentence: Microsoft says neither setting changes whether a site can appear in regular Bing results
results.evidence: Bing: 'do not change eligibility for traditional Bing search results, subject to normal crawl and indexing requirements'. Consider adding that qualifier.

results.sentence: Google says Google-Extended 'does not impact a site's inclusion in Google Search'
results.evidence: Exact: 'Google-Extended does not impact a site's inclusion in Google Search nor is it used as a ranking signal.'

results.sentence: 'This policy token is not a directive for crawling behavior,' the draft says
results.evidence: Sec 4.4 exact.

results.sentence: An AI Weekly alert notes it has 'no enforcement teeth'
results.evidence: The phrase is in AI Weekly's 'Editor's note'. AI Weekly is an aggregator; use is attributed. Prefer attributing to its editor's note.

results.sentence: Private deals between a site and an AI company can also override it
results.evidence: Sec 4.5: 'Private agreements MAY override preferences expressed via this mechanism.'

results.sentence: Signal 'says nothing about web search, AI answers, or user-triggered requests,' Vanessa Fox writes
results.evidence: Fox: 'It says nothing about web search, AI answers, or user-triggered requests.'

results.sentence: Nate Hake of Travel Lemming ... said the draft 'basically exempts the preferences from applying to anything a user does'; 'it's not actually done at the ietf level -- and some significant areas of dispute remain'
results.evidence: Both are Hake posts on X (Oct 30) embedded in the SER article. Affiliation from the draft's acknowledgments table. Quote 1 starts 'it basically exempts'; fine. Should be described as posts, not interview comments.

results.sentence: Unless a site names Google-Extended itself, Google plans to read a token opt-out 'as if the publisher had disallowed Google-Extended'
results.evidence: Exact: 'Google plans to interpret that as if the publisher had disallowed Google-Extended.'

results.sentence: Only sites that allow Google-Extended can appear in answers through grounding in Gemini Apps
results.evidence: Google: 'Websites that specifically allow Google-Extended are eligible to appear in responses and receive clicks via grounding in Gemini Apps.' It does not say 'only'.
results.fix: Google says sites that specifically allow Google-Extended are eligible to appear in Gemini Apps grounded responses.

results.sentence: So a site that opts out of training with the new token may also drop out of those answers
results.evidence: Writer's inference from Google's two statements; not stated by Google. Label as analysis.
results.fix: By Google's description, a site that opts out with the new token and does not name Google-Extended would not count as specifically allowing it, so it could lose eligibility for Gemini Apps grounded answers (our reading, not Google's statement).

results.sentence: Team led from UIUC reports dedicated memory systems often do worse than raw-history search; quote 'We find many dedicated memory systems underperform naive RAG in many cases, indicating a negative net value'
results.evidence: Abstract: 'we find many dedicated memory systems underperform naive RAG in many cases, indicating a negative net value' (lowercase 'we' in source). Authors UIUC and Tsinghua; first and senior authors UIUC.

results.sentence: Preprint posted to arXiv Oct 25 and is not yet peer-reviewed
results.evidence: arXiv: 'Submitted on 25 Oct 2026'. No venue listed, so 'not yet peer-reviewed' is the correct label.

results.sentence: It drew 157 upvotes after Hugging Face Daily Papers listed it on Oct 28
results.evidence: API: upvotes 157, submittedOnDailyAt 2026-10-28. The count is as of my fetch on Oct 31. Note the daily submission was made by author hexuan21.

results.sentence: Memory system rewrites past chats into facts, summaries or graphs; naive RAG chunks raw history, searches, hands best matches to the model
results.evidence: Paper: memory units as 'summaries, extracted facts, structured records, episodic entries'; graph-based category listed; naive RAG 'keeps raw history with minimal processing and retrieves relevant chunks directly' (BM25+dense, reranked). Definitions supported.

results.sentence: Memory benefit counts questions memory gets right that RAG misses; tax counts the reverse; when tax is bigger memory loses
results.evidence: Paper intro: memory 'solve[s] some queries RAG misses ... while losing others that RAG already solves ... When the tax outweighs the benefit, memory falls below RAG overall'.

results.sentence: Memory 'does solve some queries RAG misses,' ... 'while losing others that RAG already solves'
results.evidence: Exact fragments from the intro.

results.sentence: 90 of 99 results, 11 systems, 3 benchmarks, 3 models fell below naive RAG, per project page
results.evidence: Project page text matches. Caveat to add: the comparison line is 'RAG (2rd)' (second-round retrieval), the stronger of the two RAG baselines.

results.sentence: Models were Qwen3.5-4B, Qwen3.6-27B and GPT-5.6 Luna
results.evidence: Paper: 'GPT-5.6 Luna (low)'. Consider adding '(low reasoning setting)'.

results.sentence: 31.8 versus 72.2: widest gap, OpenViking 31.8 on LongMemEval-s with Qwen3.5-4B, RAG 72.2 (Table 1)
results.evidence: Table 1: OpenViking 31.8 (-40.4) vs 'RAG (2rd)' 72.2 on LongMemEval-s/Q3.5-4B. Largest drop of the 90 negative cells (next largest -27.0). But 72.2 is the 2-round RAG; one-round RAG is 70.2 (gap 38.4). 'RAG' alone is ambiguous.
results.fix: The widest gap: OpenViking scored 31.8 on LongMemEval-s with Qwen3.5-4B, against 72.2 for the paper's two-round RAG baseline.

results.sentence: OpenViking kept only 39.4% of sampled facts with no loss, against 98.4% for MemoryOS (Table 2)
results.evidence: Table 2 'NL' column: OpenViking 39.4, MemoryOS 98.4. (OpenViking also had 38.0% with no memory unit.)

results.sentence: Lost information 'becomes a direct cause of memory tax'; saved facts can be fragmented, diluted or rephrased
results.evidence: Paper: 'Information loss with varying severity ... becomes a direct cause of memory tax'; 'fragmented across multiple memory units, diluted with unrelated information, or rephrased'.

results.sentence: Of earlier memory papers reviewed, only three (LightMem, PlugMem, Mem-T) reported a RAG comparison
results.evidence: Paper: 'only three of them (excluding originally RAG system like HippoRAG2) report RAG results (LightMem, PlugMem, and Mem-T)'.

results.sentence: About 70%: a basic RAG-Hybrid baseline reaches that on many memory benchmarks; keyword matcher tops 50% on some
results.evidence: Paper and project page: IDF-keyword 'more than 50% ... on some of them, while RAG-Hybrid reaches about 70%' and 'simple retrieval baselines already performs quite well on some of the benchmarks'. 'Many' is not supported.
results.fix: RAG-Hybrid reaches about 70% on some of the memory benchmarks the authors checked, and a simple keyword matcher tops 50% on some.

results.sentence: The authors' fix keeps 'a lightweight path back to the source history'
results.evidence: Exact: 'preserving a lightweight path back to the source history'. Authors call it 'a simple proof of concept'; consider saying so.

results.sentence: SimpleMem 73.6 to 82.8 on LongMemEval-s with Qwen3.6-27B; tax 12.0 to 5.2
results.evidence: Project page table (Qwen3.6-27B): SimpleMem 73.6 / tax 12.0; + src-aug 82.8 / tax 5.2. Also matches Table 1 SimpleMem 73.6 (-7.8).

results.sentence: Grader is an AI judge running Qwen3.6-27B, also one of the answering models
results.evidence: Paper: 'LLM-as-Judge backed by Qwen3.6-27B'.

results.sentence: Two benchmarks tested on 20% and 10% samples 'due to cost constraints'
results.evidence: Paper: 'Due to cost constraints, we evaluate 20% of PersonaMem-v2 and 10% of MINT-Eval.'

results.sentence: PlugMem, one of the systems tested, comes from overlapping authors
results.evidence: Not in the paper [13]. PlugMem (arXiv 2603.03296) authors include Ke Yang, Xuan He, Jiawei Han, ChengXiang Zhai, all Memory Tax authors. True, but the cited source does not show it.
results.fix: Cite https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.03296 (PlugMem: A Task-Agnostic Plugin Memory Module for LLM Agents) and add it to sources.

results.sentence: Authors call their system list 'representative rather than exhaustive'; more tuning 'may yield better performance'
results.evidence: Limitations section: 'representative rather than exhaustive'; 'further system-specific tuning may yield better performance'.

results.sentence: Code to reproduce each system is not yet released
results.evidence: README TODO: '[ ] Release reproduction codes of each baseline' unchecked; results and intermediates are released. Wording 'to reproduce each system' fits.

results.sentence: On web tasks, turning long action records into workflows 'can outperform naive RAG,' though several methods fall behind on tool use
results.evidence: Paper: 'distilling long traces into workflows or strategies can outperform naive RAG, while for tool-use, several memory methods fall behind it'.

results.sentence: Bao et al.: raw-history RAG ranked first in six of seven benchmark-model settings
results.evidence: Abstract: 'Raw-RAG ranks first among the compared memory systems in six of seven benchmark-model settings'. arXiv, submitted 22 Oct 2026.

results.sentence: Yuan, Su and Yao: raw chunks, needing zero AI model calls, 'matches or outperforms expensive lossy alternatives'
results.evidence: Abstract: 'Raw chunked storage, which requires zero LLM calls, matches or outperforms expensive lossy alternatives'. Study is on LoCoMo only; accepted at ICLR 2026 MemAgents Workshop, so 'preprint' is fine but 'accepted at a workshop' is more accurate.

results.sentence: Huang et al. found 'no single substrate consistently dominates'
results.evidence: Abstract exact.

results.sentence: Vectorize: 'RAG is often the wrong tool for memory because memory queries are not just document similarity problems'
